problem: Paused native audio could remain inside the 350 ms ongoing drift deadband at play admission. Native decoder startup then added lag; fulfillment only reported ready and did not reconcile the latest shared state. The next poll could eventually repair it, but startup and isolated synchronization checks exceeded the existing threshold.

reproduction.localNativeProbe: Chromium 151: approximately 0.349 s lag at native play admission grew to approximately 0.442 s after startup. This is an individual diagnostic observation, not an asserted stable latency.
newRegressionFailuresBeforeFix: No alignment at the native play call when the shared target was 0.3 s ahead inside the deadband.
A delayed native start after a newer same-source seek retained approximately 0.594 s of advancing drift.
A delayed native start could remain playing when the shared target had reached the track endpoint.

fix: Force alignment at genuine new enabled play admission, then reconcile the current snapshot and offset after native play fulfillment. Preserve consent, source/generation ownership, source readiness and endpoint behavior. Do not await the attempt's own pending synchronization promise. Ongoing 350 ms correction and original assertions are unchanged.

verification.independentSourceReview: No actionable findings; reviewed implementation and all seven new native regressions.
verification.localSuiteIsolation: The ordinary browser service port 4220 was occupied. Temporary copies of specs/config changed only that port to 4224 and resolved the sync HTML fixture by its absolute path. Real service, FFmpeg normalization and native audio were retained; no tracked configuration was changed or unidentified process stopped.
verification.ciBrowserTests: 23 passed in 34.5 s on the unchanged CI configuration

newCases: Alignment at the exact native play call while starting inside the normal drift deadband.
Delayed start uses a newer same-source seek and advancing wall-clock target.
Pending startup preserves a newer shared pause.
Pending startup preserves locally disabled audio.
Pending startup preserves a newer paused source.
Delayed startup pauses at the reached shared endpoint.
An older native startup cannot pause a newer playing source.
limitations: Tests establish the local Chromium protocol with actual media decoding and controlled scheduling of native play. They do not establish arbitrary-network synchronization, physical output-device latency, subjective listening quality, or other browser support.
